sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first. The instance fetches and caches all three keys, starts the refresh timer, and only then binds the HTTP port. It is ready (/healthz 200) only after the keys are loaded and the server is running.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. It never listens or becomes ready, so the rollout halts. Old v1 pods keep serving, so there is no customer impact.
sonnet.q3: A timer every 300 seconds (with small jitter) fetches all three secrets. If a version id changed, it swaps in the new value and logs 'rotated <name> to version <id>'. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (secret name, version id in use, error class, no values), and retries next cycle.
sonnet.q4: Held only in the in-memory key cache. They must never appear in logs, repr, exception text, tracebacks, HTTP debug output (Authorization header or request body), environment variables, temp files, on-disk cache or subprocesses. Version ids may be logged.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod workload identity (orders-api/prod/* only). Write: only the security on-call role. Engineers cannot read or list prod.
sonnet.q6: Git stores the file, so key A stays in git history, and the document says history is not rewritten. Old v1 images also still contain it. Key A is treated as leaked. What makes the old values harmless is revoking key A at each provider (Step 9), after which copies left behind have no customer impact.
sonnet.q7: Clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) hold a reference to the key cache, not a copy. Each provider call reads the current value from the cache. A call already in progress keeps the value it read.
sonnet.q8: In Step 8 the team confirms all 4 pods run the v2 digest, each pod logged its version ids at startup, and the provider 401/403 rate is at baseline, after a soak period. Step 9 also requires no pod running the v1 digest, no consumer using key A, and dev and CI using no live keys.
sonnet.q9: Order is: set store access policy (Step 2), then create key B at providers and write it to the store (Step 5, rotating at providers), with the code change built on a branch beforehand (Step 4) that removes api_key from the file. Then merge to main and build v2 (Step 6), so the removal lands only at merge. Then roll out v2, which reads from the store (Step 7). Key A is revoked at the providers last (Step 9).
sonnet.q10: From dev values in the store at orders-api/dev/*, which hold sandbox keys. They are loaded through the same loader using the engineer's own identity. Local runs never use live keys. Offline mode uses stub clients with no network or store access. How engineers authenticate for dev reads is not specified.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document only says a failed fetch is retried 3 times, then the instance exits non-zero, and that it binds the port only after all keys are loaded. It does not describe a missing secret specifically.
sonnet.q12: No schedule is set. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate. The refresh mechanism would support any cadence without a restart.
